parts.t: Langley condos sit in a few clear pockets: the newer low-rises and towers of Willoughby, Latimer and Carvolth, the established streets of Walnut Grove, the quieter village feel of Murrayville, and the walkable core of Langley City. Each one lives differently, from Highway 1 access near 202 Street to shops and the future SkyTrain downtown. Below are the current listings, with a short guide to each area after them.

blocks.text: Where Langley condos are, area by area

parts.t: This is where much of the new condo building in the Township has happened. You will find four- to six-storey wood-frame buildings and some taller concrete towers, with many recent completions. Streets are laid out around 200 Street and 208 Street, with shops, cafes and grocery stores close by. Carvolth sits next to Highway 1 and the Carvolth Exchange park-and-ride on 202 Street, where express buses connect toward SkyTrain, which helps if you commute west. It suits first-time buyers, young couples, and anyone who wants a newer building, possibly with some home warranty coverage still in place.

Walnut Grove is an older, settled part of the Township. Its condo buildings are generally older than Willoughby's, and some offer larger floor plans than newer suites. Parks, trails and schools are woven through the neighbourhood, and Highway 1 is close by for trips in either direction. It suits buyers who want more square footage per dollar and do not mind an older building, as long as the strata paperwork checks out.

Murrayville is smaller and calmer, on the east side of Langley's urban area along Fraser Highway. Langley Memorial Hospital, at 22051 Fraser Highway, is a short drive away. There are fewer condo buildings here, so choice can be thin at times. Many owners like the slower pace and the older trees. It suits downsizers, hospital staff, and people who want a quiet street over a busy town centre.
Langley City

Langley City is its own municipality, surrounded by the Township on three sides and bordered by Surrey on the west. Most of its condos sit near Fraser Highway and the downtown core, within walking distance of shops, restaurants and bus routes. It is also where the future Langley City Centre SkyTrain station is going. For a closer look at downtown, the Nicomekl floodplain trails and the SkyTrain area, see the
City of Langley condos page

blocks.text: Which part of Langley has the newest condos?

parts.t: Willoughby, Latimer and Carvolth have most of the newer buildings. Some recent buildings may still carry home warranty coverage. Always confirm the warranty details for the exact building.

blocks.text: Are Walnut Grove condos older than Willoughby condos?

parts.t: Generally, yes. Older buildings can mean bigger suites, but it is worth reading the depreciation report and strata minutes closely.

blocks.text: What is the difference between Langley City and the Township of Langley?

parts.t: They are two separate municipalities. Langley City is the smaller urban core along Fraser Highway. The Township is much larger and includes Willoughby, Walnut Grove, Murrayville, Fort Langley and the rural areas.

blocks.text: What should I check before buying a Langley condo?

parts.t: Look at the strata bylaws, the depreciation report, recent strata minutes, the Form B information certificate and the contingency reserve fund. These show the building's health and any rules on pets or parking. Looking at an older building downtown? See my list of
things to check in older City buildings

blocks.text: Will the SkyTrain reach the Township of Langley?

parts.t: The
Surrey Langley SkyTrain

will end at Langley City Centre station, east of 203 Street and Industrial Avenue. Willowbrook station, at the northeast corner of 196 Street and Fraser Highway, will serve Surrey, the Township and the City, which all meet at that spot. The Province expects service to start in late 2029.
